title: Mate with the Queen
subtitle: Box in the king, bring your own, deliver mate.
goals: Build the queen's box a knight's-move away

steps.say: Queen versus lone king is the mate you'll deliver most often — but the queen can't do it alone, and one careless move gives stalemate. The method: the queen boxes the king in from a knight's-move away, your king walks over, and together they finish.
The magic trick: keep the queen a KNIGHT'S move away from their king.

autoMoves.say: A knight's-move from the king. From here the queen fences him in — he can never cross her lines.
The king stepped back — the queen follows, knight's-move away again. Every move, the box shrinks. No checks needed yet!

steps.prompt: The king retreated to c7. Shrink the box — place the queen a knight's move away again.
hints: From c7, a knight would reach a6, b5, d5, e6... your queen wants one of those squares.
Two queen moves keep the pattern: one on the a-file, one in the center.

line.say: Knight's-move away — the king is squeezed toward the corner and the queen is untouchable.
Knight's-move away — the box tightens and the king drifts to the edge.

rejections.say: Kxb6! You parked the queen right next to the king with no support. The knight's-move distance exists precisely so this can never happen.
Kxc6! Adjacent to the enemy king with no defender — the queen is just food there. Keep the knight's-move distance.

steps.wrongSay: Picture a knight standing on the black king's square — your queen belongs on one of ITS squares.
steps.successSay: That spacing does everything: boxes the king, stays safe, and never risks stalemate.

steps.prompt: The king is cornered — the box is perfect. The queen's work is done: bring your KING into the fight!
hints: The queen alone can never mate — she needs her king beside her. And careful: sealing the last square without check is stalemate!
Leave the queen exactly where she is. March your king toward the corner.

line.say: The king marches! The queen holds the cage; the king brings the handcuffs.
Onward! A few more steps and the king joins the mating net.
The king starts his walk — the queen holds the fort until he arrives.

rejections.say: STALEMATE!! The queen now covers a7 as well — the king has NO move and is NOT in check. A completely won game, instantly drawn. Always leave the boxed king one free square until mate.
Kxb7! Right next to the king, undefended, again. The queen keeps her distance until your own king protects her.

steps.wrongSay: The box is already perfect — improving it risks stalemate. This is a KING move.
steps.successSay: Queen boxes, king walks. Remember the rhythm — and remember what Qb6 would have done!

steps.prompt: Your king has arrived. Checkmate in one — and beware the stalemate trap!
hints: Your king covers b7 and b8. The queen must attack a8 AND a7 in the same move.
One line on the board covers both of those squares — the a-file.

line.say: Checkmate! The queen owns the whole a-file — a8 checked, a7 sealed — while your king guards b7 and b8. Textbook teamwork.

rejections.say: STALEMATE! You sealed a7 without giving check — no moves, no check, draw. The winning move covers a7 and CHECKS a8 at the same time.
Check — but only along the back rank. The king slips out to a7. You need one move that covers the corner AND its neighbor.

steps.wrongSay: Find the line that hits a8 and a7 together — check and cage in one.
steps.successSay: King-and-queen mate complete. This exact finish will close out hundreds of your games.
